method: Real rendered Minecraft client and integrated server, copied flat world, one named NPC held nearby. Synthetic messages enter AiChatService.chat on the server thread; legacy uses actual event-template speech. Models sequentially reloaded through AiChatService.start, managed llama-server per model. Windows GetProcessMemoryInfo sampled every 500ms; native peak uses the OS lifetime peak for each fresh native process.
limitations: One short run per variant, three direct prompts each plus any automatic events; not a complete gameplay or quality evaluation.
Measured native resident peak is additional to Minecraft. Java and combined figures include the whole game, world and test driver; they are not the mod-only cost.
Working set, private committed bytes, Java heap and disk size are different metrics. Exact recorded bytes describe this run only, not a universal RAM requirement.
Other applications were running; free physical RAM was about 1.2 GiB during the legacy baseline. OS paging/cache and workload change resident usage.
Profile changes reuse one Minecraft process; Java memory drift and garbage collection prevent attributing total-game differences solely to model choice.
Scripted chat exercises the mod service but does not simulate keyboard typing, menu clicks, network authentication or multiplayer signing.
This is the current 1.20.1 workspace, not the separately named CurseForge 1.21.1 instance.

quality_observations: All completed stages must be judged on actual replies, not merely the ready status. Zero inference errors does not prove relevance or action correctness.
Standard SmolLM2 answered a greeting with "8 Bread, you said?"; standard Qwen3 answered a bread request with "Crouch twice, not rn". These are off-topic despite valid generated output.

Qwen2.5 standard said "2 Bread, here you go", but the recorded player bread count remained zero. This run did not demonstrate a successful gift transaction; text alone must not be reported as a verified transfer.
The final Qwen3.5 Unfiltered stage increased the player bread count from zero to two. A two-bread transfer was verified in that stage.
Only short greeting/work/item scenarios were exercised. Combat, damage, lifecycle replies, chest ownership, language quality and long-session memory behavior were not comprehensively tested.
